 Order

The petitioner has filed this petition under Section 439 of Code of Criminal Procedure seeking bail in Crime No.62/2022 dated 24.12.2022 registered by the Yadgiri Women Police Station, Yadgir for the offences punishable under Sections 341, 363, 376 and 506 of Indian Penal Code and Section 4 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012.

entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: 2. The factual matrix of the prosecution case are that, the complainant-victim is a student of ninth standard residing backside of Degree college at Yadgir.
The accused/petitioner is known to her brother Shaik Mannan.
Therefore, the petitioner voluntarily used to come to the house of the victim and used to talk with her.
Later whenever the victim used to go to school, the petitioner used to follow her on his motorbike and forcing her to love him but she used to reply that still she is a minor.
Later the petitioner gave one mobile phone to the victim girl and asked her to talk with him as he was deeply loved with her.
Accordingly, the complainant-victim and petitioner are used to talk each other through mobile phone No.7829640546 which was provided by him.

It is further alleged that on 12.12.2022 at about 1.30 p.m. when the victim was returning from her school for lunch, the petitioner came on his Bajaj Pulsar motorbike and stopped in front of her and asked her to sit on the motorbike and when she refused, he gave life threat to her and thus due to fear she went along with the petitioner on his motorbike to Gurumitkal and went in a room wherein the petitioner forcibly committed sexual intercourse with her.
Thereafter, returned at 5.30 p.m. and dropped her near degree college at Yadgir.
It is alleged that the petitioner has given life threat to her if she disclosed the incident to anyone.
Hence, after lapse of 11 days i.e., on 23.12.2022 the victim disclosed the incident to her parents and lodged complaint against the petitioner and FIR has been lodged against him as stated supra.
During the course of investigation, the respondent police arrested the petitioner on 28.12.2022.
Eversince then he is in judicial custody.
Being aggrieved by the same, he approached the Sessions Court/Special Court, Yadgiri for grant of bail in Special Case No.13/2023 which came to be rejected vide order dated 11.04.2023.
Hence, the petitioner before this Court for grant of regular bail.
3. I have heard the learned counsel for the petitioner and the learned High Court Government Pleader for respondent/State and perused the materials available on record.

4. Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that both victim and the petitioner are residing in the same lane and if the petitioner is really and forcibly given the mobile to the victim, then her parents,
friends and relatives ought to have enquired about using of mobile.
He would further contend that the victim voluntarily accompanied the petitioner in his motorbike and went to Gurumitkal town.

sentences.text: Since they were loving each other, there is no such incident of kidnap or forcible sexual intercourse as committed by the petitioner.
Hence, he prays to enlarge the petitioner on bail.

5. Today the learned counsel for the petitioner produced the whatsapp details between the petitioner and the victim girl and contend that they both are fell in love and the victim girl accompanied the petitioner and there is no such sexual act committed by the petitioner.
As such, he prays to enlarge the petitioner on bail.

6. Per contra, learned High Court Government Pleader vehemently contended that complaint averments and the 164 statement of the victim girl clearly makes out a prima facie case against the petitioner and the victim being the minor, the petitioner is not entitled for grant bail.
7. Having heard the counsel for the petitioner and the learned High Court Government Pleader and perused the records.

8. On careful perusal of the complaint and 164 statement of the victim girl it could be gathered that the petitioner and the victim girl are loving each other and even the whatsapp chats records produced by the learned counsel for the petitioner which reveals that they were loving each other and chatting through whatsapp.
Admittedly, there is a delay of 11 days in lodging the complaint.
In the circumstances, as per the law laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Uday vs. State of Karnataka1.
Relevant paragraph No.21 is extracted below :-
"...... there is no strait jacket formula for determining whether consent given by the prosecutrix to sexual intercourse is voluntary, or whether it is given under a misconception of fact.

In the ultimate analysis, the tests laid down by the Courts provide at best guidance to the judicial mind while considering a question of consent,
but the Court must, in each case, consider the evidence before it and the surrounding circumstances, before reaching a conclusion, because each case has its own peculiar facts which may have a bearing on the question whether the consent was voluntary,
or was given under a misconception of fact.
It must also weigh the evidence keeping in view the fact that the burden is on the prosecution to prove each and every ingredient of the offence, absence of consent being one of them."
Therefore, in the present case on hand, it is voluntary consent or consent under misconception of fact has to be decided during trial.
However, the fact whether the petitioner intends to have decisive the complaint from inception, it would amounts [(2003) 4 Supreme Court Cases 46] for consideration at the time of trial.
Therefore, the incarceration of the petitioner would lead to a miscarriage of justice.
The petitioner has made out a case to enlarge him on bail.

Hence, the following:
ORDER
The petition filed under Section 439 of Cr.P.C. is allowed.

Consequently, the petitioner/accused shall be released on bail in connection with Crime No.62/2022 dated 24.12.2022 registered by the Yadgiri Women Police Station,
